name: auth
description: Full authentication with Better Auth on Elysia: email/password, sessions, OAuth, organizations, passkeys, API keys, and optional two-factor policies. Installs a secure-by-default request guard.
env: # BETTER_AUTH_SECRET also derives the key that encrypts config secrets stored in the
# DB (OAuth client secrets, SMTP password). Keep it stable and secret; rotating it
# makes previously saved DB secrets undecryptable.
# Everything below is optional. OAuth providers, SMTP, and server-enforced
# toggles are configured on the admin Settings page and applied without restart.
# Email/SMTP is provided by the mailer module (see its .env block).

inject.text:
### auth (Better Auth + Elysia)
- The API is secure by default: every application route needs a session except health, OpenAPI, `/api/auth/*`, and routes explicitly registered in `ACCESS_POLICY`.
- Register a public route during module configuration with `services.resolve(ACCESS_POLICY).register("GET", "/path", "public")`; use `AUTH` and `AuthService.requireSession()` or `requireAdmin()` when a handler needs the current user.
- Configure OAuth providers, SMTP, sign-up approval, automatic logout, and server toggles on the admin Settings page. Only `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` and `BETTER_AUTH_URL` are required environment variables.
- Use `{{apiRun}} auth:configure{{apiWorkspaceArg}} -- ...` and `.claude/skills/podokit-configure-auth` to apply OAuth/SMTP credentials without committing secrets.
- Run `bun run --cwd apps/api migrate:all` in development and production so Better Auth and application migrations use the versions installed by the app.

instructions: Set BETTER_AUTH_SECRET in .env (at least 32 characters). Keep it stable because it also protects encrypted DB configuration secrets.
Create the Better Auth and application tables: bun run --cwd apps/api migrate:all
Run the same migration command after building a production image: bun run --cwd apps/api migrate:all
Sign up: curl -c cookies.txt -XPOST localhost:5002/api/auth/sign-up/email -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"email":"a@example.com","password":"password123","name":"A"}'
Call a protected route with the session: curl -b cookies.txt localhost:5002/account/me
Use {{apiRun}} auth:configure{{apiWorkspaceArg}} -- --help for redacted OAuth, SMTP, and sign-up approval automation.
Routes are protected by default. Register intentional public or API-key routes in ACCESS_POLICY during module configuration.
